skill.name: cost-guard
skill.description: Estimate one-time and recurring AI costs, compare recorded spend with local budgets, and flag repeated failures before retrying.
skill.summary: Local cost estimates and budget checks for AI coding workflows.
skill.author: kml11kml

security_audit.summary: The static alerts identify documented local file access, scoped settings, and Markdown examples. No evidence found of credential harvesting, network transmission by the scripts, or prompt injection. The audit found gaps in hook coverage, numeric validation, concurrent ledger updates, and preservation of existing budget settings.

remediation.issue: The sample hook checks only previously recorded daily spend before Bash calls.
remediation.suggestion: Label the sample as a Bash-only check of recorded spend. Require an explicit task label and projected cost for preflight decisions.

remediation.issue: Concurrent writers can lose spend or failure records.
remediation.suggestion: Lock the full read, update, and write transaction or use a transactional database. Test simultaneous spend and failure records.

remediation.issue: The check accepts invalid budget inputs.
remediation.suggestion: Reject nonfinite or negative projected costs, caps, rates, and ledger costs. Require a positive integer retry limit.

remediation.issue: The example configuration copy can reset existing budgets.
remediation.suggestion: Create the configuration only if it does not exist. Tell returning users how to review or merge defaults without replacing their limits.

semantic_findings.title: Sample hook does not check projected or per-task spend
semantic_findings.description: The example only runs a bare budget check before Bash calls. With no task or projected cost, it cannot stop a step that would cross a cap.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The hook passes no arguments beyond the check command. The parser defaults to no task and zero projected cost.

semantic_findings.title: Concurrent ledger updates can erase records
semantic_findings.description: Parallel sessions can load the same ledger, then each replace it with a different update. Lost records can understate spend or delay the retry warning.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both commands load and save separately without a lock. Atomic replacement prevents a partial file but does not merge concurrent updates.

semantic_findings.title: Invalid numeric inputs can defeat budget checks
semantic_findings.description: The check accepts negative or nonfinite cost estimates. Invalid estimates can understate projected spend or prevent a comparison from blocking the run.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parser accepts unrestricted floats, and the cap checks use greater-than comparisons. The environment helper also accepts nonfinite cap values.

semantic_findings.title: Setup can replace existing budget settings
semantic_findings.description: Repeating the optional configuration setup can overwrite an existing file and restore limits that the user did not choose.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The copy does not check whether the destination exists. The script uses that file for budget settings unless an override applies.

content.user_title: Estimate and Track AI Coding Costs
content.value_statement: Long coding sessions and recurring jobs can use more tokens than expected. Cost Guard estimates spend and checks your local records against budgets before you proceed.
actual_capabilities: Estimate one-time costs from supplied input, output, and cache-read token counts using configurable rates.
Project daily runs, token use, and time to exhaust a supplied weekly allowance for recurring jobs.
Record estimated spend locally and show daily totals and totals for a selected task today.
Check whether a projected cost plus recorded spend would exceed the daily or selected task budget.
Count recorded failures with the same signature each day and flag when the configured retry threshold is reached.
Provide optional Claude Code hooks for session status and a daily budget check before Bash calls.
limitations: The tools do not read provider bills, quotas, or live token usage. Runs you do not record are absent from budget checks.
Per-task totals cover the current local day. The shared ledger can lose records when updated concurrently.
The sample hook checks recorded daily spend before Bash calls only. It cannot stop model requests and does not run per-task or projected-cost checks.
Built-in rates can become outdated, and recurring estimates do not account for extra retries or overlapping jobs unless you adjust the inputs.

use_cases.title: Budget a large code change
use_cases.description: Estimate a refactor from expected token counts and compare it with the budget for that task today.

use_cases.title: Compare schedules for a recurring job
use_cases.description: Compare token demand at two intervals and estimate how long a supplied weekly allowance would last.

use_cases.title: Set a retry threshold
use_cases.description: Record repeated validation failures under one signature and pause when the threshold is reached.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate one run
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate the cost for Sonnet with one million input tokens and 500,000 output tokens. Show the rates used and do not start the work.

prompt_templates.title: Check today's budget
prompt_templates.prompt: Show today's recorded spend for the docs task. Check whether another $2.50 would exceed the daily or task budget. Stop and ask before proceeding if blocked.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Check a planned step against local totals.

prompt_templates.title: Track repeated failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Record this checkout test failure under the same signature as earlier attempts. Report the count and pause for approval if the retry threshold is reached.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Review a repeat failure before trying again.

prompt_templates.title: Compare recurring job scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare 15-minute and 60-minute schedules for eight active hours per day. Use 20,000 tokens per run, a 1.25 retry multiplier, and a two-million-token weekly allowance. Report daily runs, daily tokens, and days to exhaust the allowance without scheduling anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Evaluate recurring workloads before activation.

output_examples.input: Estimate a Sonnet run with one million input tokens, 500,000 output tokens, and no cache reads.
output_examples.output: Estimated cost: $10.50 using the bundled Sonnet rates. Actual charges may differ.

output_examples.input: Check a $2.50 step when the task has recorded $3.20 today and the $5 task budget is the limiting cap.
output_examples.output: Budget check blocked. The task would reach $5.70, which exceeds its $5 budget.

output_examples.input: Estimate an hourly job that runs eight hours daily, uses 20,000 tokens per run, and has a 1.25 retry multiplier and two-million-token weekly allowance.
output_examples.output: Eight scheduled runs and 200,000 estimated tokens per day. The supplied allowance would last 10 days at that rate.

best_practices: Verify current rates and use realistic inputs for retries, overlap, and active hours.
Record finished runs promptly and use a consistent task label for estimates and checks.
Review the optional hooks before enabling them and keep provider-side spending controls in place.
anti_patterns: Treating an estimate or the local ledger as a statement of actual charges.
Assuming the sample Bash hook enforces a per-task limit or stops model calls.
Reusing the same failure signature for unrelated problems or changing it between retries of the same failure.

faq.question: Does it read my provider bill or plan quota?
faq.answer: No. It calculates estimates from token counts and rates you supply or configure.

faq.question: What are the default budgets and retry limit?
faq.answer: The defaults are $10 per day, $5 per task per day, and three recorded failures with the same signature in one day.

faq.question: Do the hooks stop model calls or all tool calls?
faq.answer: No. The sample checks recorded daily spend before Bash calls and reports status at session start and stop.

faq.question: Does it log every run or retry automatically?
faq.answer: No. The workflow must explicitly record token counts and failure signatures.

faq.question: Can I use the calculators outside Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The Python calculators run locally with supplied inputs. The included hook definitions are specific to Claude Code.

faq.question: Where are the budget settings and records stored?
faq.answer: By default, the skill uses separate configuration and ledger files in the .cost-guard folder in your home directory.
